In an online meeting, your own speech and the other side's are now transcribed separately, so 評分 scores only what you said. Dropdowns also scroll properly again.

**Your side and theirs, kept apart** (#689)

- During an online meeting, your microphone and the computer's audio are transcribed as two separate streams. Your microphone is always you, and the computer audio is always the other side, so the 評分 report no longer has to guess which speaker you are.
- Speakers are named by side: 我 (or 我 1, 我 2 when several people share your microphone), and 遠端 1, 遠端 2 on the far side. Several voices on either side are still told apart.
- Turn-taking, response time, interruptions and the talk-time split now work for these meetings too.
- Without headphones, your speakers can leak the other side into your microphone. Parley drops a line of yours when it repeats what the other side just said at the same moment. Short replies such as 對 or OK are always kept.
- The recording still holds both sides, and playback has both. Before, a meeting transcribed without speaker separation recorded only your microphone.
- Analyses saved before this update still resolve their old speaker labels.

**Dropdowns scroll** (#691)

- In the desktop app, a long dropdown such as Settings › Transcription's provider list stopped short and wouldn't scroll with the mouse wheel or trackpad. Dropdowns now open below their button and scroll normally.
